component.title: Who owns what in the working-surface architecture?
component.concern: Separate domain truth, Representation Router contracts, product-owned behavior, and human judgment so the diagram does not imply authority the router does not have.

nodes.title: Domain / workflow truth
nodes.summary: Company Planning, DoDAF, Git/code, runtime, tests, or product-domain state remains authoritative outside the router.

nodes.title: ViewSpec
nodes.summary: One concern-specific semantic projection, representation, interaction, availability, provenance, and success criteria.

nodes.title: SurfaceSpec
nodes.summary: Coordinates one or more ViewSpecs, exact source revisions, shared focus, interface patterns, provenance, and action boundaries.

nodes.title: Product-owned application
nodes.summary: Renderer, persistence, authorization, workflow effects, and final interaction behavior remain product-owned.

nodes.title: Evidence / CI
nodes.summary: Exact execution receipts support claims but do not grant semantic or human-review authority.

nodes.title: Human reviewer
nodes.summary: Plans, inspects, learns, reviews, operates, or decides through the working representation.

sequence.title: How does a verified change become a human-reviewable representation?
sequence.concern: Show the ordered machine and human handoffs without treating a successful automated check as the human decision.

messages.label: pin merged change + source revisions
messages.note: The model is grounded in immutable PR #22/merge evidence.

messages.label: provide concepts, requirements, evidence, provenance
messages.note: Renderer receives representation data; it does not invent semantic membership.

messages.label: execute build
messages.note: CI invokes the deterministic self-contained workbench build.

messages.label: emit self-contained HTML artifact
messages.note: The output contains the review data and interactions with no runtime network dependency.

messages.label: publish verified artifact
messages.note: A successful artifact build means the representation was produced; it does not mean the reviewer accepts it.

messages.label: inspect component / sequence / state / evidence
messages.note: Human navigates concern-specific views while retaining provenance.

messages.label: show explanation + provenance + nonclaims
messages.note: The surface supports judgment but does not perform the judgment.

state.title: What gates a software change from implementation to human acceptance?
state.concern: Keep machine verification, merge/build status, and human acceptance as distinct states with explicit transition authority.

states.label: Planned
states.summary: Outcome and bounded change are recorded.

states.label: Implemented
states.summary: Schema, builder, docs, and tests exist in the reviewed revision.

states.label: Merged / built
states.summary: Technical delivery is integrated and a review artifact can be generated.

states.label: Human review
states.summary: A person evaluates comprehension, usefulness, correctness beyond automated checks, or product acceptance.

states.label: Changes requested
states.summary: Human identifies a concrete revision needed before acceptance.

state.nonclaim: There is deliberately no transition from Machine verified directly to Accepted. Green CI is evidence, not human acceptance.
